name: The Hunter's Path
summary: In Mulgore, young tauren hunters are sent to Bloodhoof Village for advanced training. There, they seek Yaw Sharpmane and begin the trials of taming and bonding with wild beasts.

sections.title: A Rite of Passage
sections.body: Among the Shu'halo, hunting is sacred. A hunter learns the balance of nature, honors the spirits of the plains, and respects the animals that sustain the tribes. When young hunters prove they can survive in the wild and use a bow or gun, their elders send them to seasoned mentors. That journey marks their step beyond solitary tracking and toward adulthood in tauren culture.

sections.title: The Road to Bloodhoof Village
sections.body: The road crosses Mulgore's grasslands to Bloodhoof Village, beside Stonebull Lake. There, Yaw Sharpmane teaches hunters about the local beasts. Meeting him marks a hunter's readiness for the trials of beast taming, where they learn to commune with predators as well as hunt them.

faq.q: What is the purpose of The Hunter's Path?
faq.answer: The Hunter's Path sends novice tauren hunters to Bloodhoof Village to begin their beast-taming trials. There, they speak with Yaw Sharpmane, who oversees the rituals for bonding with an animal companion.

faq.q: Who sends you on this quest?
faq.answer: Tauren hunter trainers send aspiring hunters once they have mastered the basics of survival and marksmanship. Kary Thunderhorn in Thunder Bluff is one such trainer.
Yaw Sharpmane is a respected tauren hunter trainer in Bloodhoof Village. He teaches young hunters to approach, calm, and tame Mulgore's wild beasts.

faq.q: What happens after completing this quest?
faq.answer: After speaking with Yaw Sharpmane, you begin the 'Taming the Beast' trials. You venture into the wild with a taming rod and pacify several native creatures before earning the right to train a permanent companion.

faq.q: Why do tauren hunters bond with beasts instead of just hunting them?
faq.answer: Tauren tradition holds that beasts are kindred spirits of the Earth Mother. A bonded animal is a companion and partner on the hunt, sharing in mutual respect and survival on the plains.

faq.q: Can hunters of other races take this specific quest?
aliases: can orcs do hunters path tauren
faq.answer: This path is for tauren hunters training in Mulgore. Other Horde races, such as orcs and trolls, receive similar training directions in their home territories in Durotar.

angles.text: As a hunter, you take your first step from archer or rifleman toward becoming a beastmaster with a loyal companion at your side.
As one of the Shu'halo, you learn to tame wild beasts as an expression of reverence for nature and the Earth Mother's creation.
As a Horde hunter, you rely on fierce frontier beasts to defend the front line and track through Kalimdor's harsh wilderness.
